explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/756: 'Bhowmick [Bh24] constructs a set of n points in R^2 such that ⌊n/4⌋ distances occur at least n+1 times.' The Lean statement says that for every n there is a Finset A ⊂ ℝ² with |A| = n and at least n/4 (natural division, i.e. the floor) elements in richDistances A (n+1), the distances determined by A whose distanceMultiplicity is ≥ n+1. distanceMultiplicity counts ordered off-diagonal pairs at distance d and halves, i.e. unordered pairs, which is the intended count. The statement is quantified over all n rather than large n; I checked the linked formal proof (plby/lean-proofs Erdos756.lean, theorem erdos756), which proves the same claim for every n (trivial cases for n < 4), so no small-n issue arises. Faithful.
